summary: The note surveys adult education programs at community colleges as of September 2023, covering new flexible and online offerings, affordability efforts, tailored curricula, industry partnerships, digital literacy, and inclusivity. It highlights named colleges, staff, and learner success stories to illustrate how these programs help adults upgrade skills, change careers, or pursue interests. The overarching theme is lifelong learning as empowerment.
one_line: Overview of 2023 community college adult education programs, their flexible formats, affordability, partnerships, digital skills, inclusivity, and learner success stories.
key_facts: Jackson Community College (JCC) launched its revamped Adult Learning Programs on September 1, 2023; Dean Laura Martin said, "No one is too old to learn."
Smithson Community College (SCC) introduced night and weekend classes for working adults; coordinator John Peterson said on September 5 that flexible schedules are key.
Franklin Adult Education Center is cited as using state funding, private donations, and strategic partnerships to make learning affordable.
Scholarship recipient Pamela Rodriguez began classes in the fall and said the new financial aid program changed her life.
Milton Community College reported record enrollment in its online adult education programs as of September 15.

Edison Community College introduced the "Life Skills for the 21st Century" module on October 1, developed by Dr. Erin Thompson, covering critical thinking, emotional intelligence, and cross-cultural communication.
Brownsville Community College began industry partnerships on September 10; community liaison Marcus Lowell said students benefit from internships and mentorship with partner companies.
Jane Campbell, president of the Adult Learners Association at Parkside Community College, is a mother of two returning to college who praised the support network.
Riverside Community College's "Digital Literacy for Adults" program kicked off on September 20; instructor Michael Donovan leads technology instruction.
Susan Lee, 45, enrolled in the culinary arts program at Hamilton Community College and now runs her own small catering business.
Tom Richardson completed a network security certification at Central Community College and secured a job at a leading tech firm.
Harrison Community College announced its "Education for All" initiative to serve underrepresented and non-traditional learners, including minorities, immigrants, and people with disabilities.
